newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Investors show buying interest.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Investors show buying interest.

text.p: Investors showed buying interest in U.S. corporate bonds on Monday, though trading was sluggish and typical of August market doldrums, traders said.
"With the Treasury market down on Friday, we saw better retail buying," said one investment-grade bond trader.
The trader said an expected slowdown in new issuance of high-grade bonds this week was also drawing investor attention to the secondary market.
"Prices are firm, but volume is still low--a lot of people are out on vacation," the trader said.
Trading in the junk bond market was similarly dead, with prices on most bonds ending unchanged on lackluster trading, market players said.
In issue-specific news, ITT Corp launched its previously announced cash tender offer for roughly $2 billion in outstanding debt on Monday.

The company said final prices for the tender offer would be determined two business days prior to the expiration date. But traders said the company and offering manager Goldman Sachs & Co were telling investors that bids would be similar to current market prices.

Traders speculated that most bondholders would be satisfied given that the current market price was substantially higher than where the bonds were trading prior to the announcement. For example, spreads on the company's 6.75 percent notes of '05 tightened to 70-60 basis points from 110-105 prior to the tender offer, on trader noted.

ITT's tender offer was part of an effort to thwart a hostile takeover by rival Hilton Hotels. The company also plans to buy back up to 30 million shares of its common stock and split itself into three seperate entities.
Elsewhere, junk bonds led the way in new issue activity.
Fedders North America Inc sold $100 million in 144a debt guaranteed by Fedders Corp (FJC.N via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. The company priced the notes (B2/B) to yield 9.45 percent.
Fedders, based in Liberty Corner, N.J., manufactures room air conditioners.
A unit of James Cable Partners LP sold $100 million in 144a seven-year senior notes via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp. The company priced the debt, rated B2/B-plus, to yield 10.75 percent.
In other markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 30.89 points higher at 8062.11
Also on Monday, the price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 2/32 to 96-18/32. Its yield rose to 6.64 percent.
